speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: I want to assure the Members that in the coming months, EnterpriseSG (ESG) will be working very closely with the industry, seeking industry feedback on the Energy Efficiency Grant (EEG) as part of our ongoing engagements with the industry, Trade Associations and Chambers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: We certainly encourage companies to adopt a "total solution" approach towards energy efficiency, as suggested by the Member.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: We welcome suggestions on how we can further help our SMEs become more energy efficient.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Together, we can make the Singapore economy more sustainable.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: In addition, food services businesses use a wide range of equipment and some of them could be very energy intensive.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Will MTI consider widening the range of equipment considered, as this could be helpful to many businesses and reduce potential equipment wastage?

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I want to thank the Member, Mr Edward Chia, for his two supplementary questions.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: And I want to assure him that MTI and ESG are very committed to work with the other Ministries and agencies to support our SMEs, to make the green transformation at the system level for those who are prepared to do so.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: But we also recognise that there are some SMEs who need to take the first baby steps and this is why we have the Energy Efficiency Grant.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: The EEG is one of the latest schemes amongst the suite of many other measures – between MTI, MSE, NEA and so on – we have in place to support our businesses to become more energy-efficient.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I want to assure him that we are committed to help our SMEs in their sustainability journey.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: So, we have that for SMEs that are prepared to go upstream to really embark on their sustainability journey at the system level.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Other than that, for our industrial SMEs, if they are keen to also go upstream and make a system level green transformation and they do not quite know what to do, they can approach EETC.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: This is a collaboration between NEA and one of our Autonomous University (AU), Singapore Institute of Technology (SIT).

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: So, what can they do for the SMEs?

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: They will help them provide energy audits, because you need to start with knowing how much energy you are consuming, the whole of the organisation, your production lines and so on.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: They will also help SMEs build up their local energy efficiency capabilities.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: And if the SME has Research Scientist Engineers (RSE), they can also work in tandem with them to upskill their engineers and practitioners in energy efficiency.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: On the Member's second question about why the six, can we go beyond the six categories?

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Allow me to take a step back and share why the three sectors, and then, why these six categories?

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: In MTI and ESG, we have been working very closely with our industries, with our SMEs, across all sectors and we know that in the last nine months, it has been difficult, in particular, our SMEs in the food services, food manufacturing and the retail sectors.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: We know that they tend to have a larger electricity component in their overall business costs.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Because we work very closely with NEA's licensing department to pre-approve the equipment, so that the SME applicants will be able to adopt this energy efficient appliances and equipment readily, very quickly and easily as well.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Essentially, these six categories are identified based on two key considerations.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Number one, what would be the energy efficient technologies behind, whether it is the cooker, hob, refrigerators and so on.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: We would like to invite them to make the submission to apply for the review and we certainly will evaluate accordingly.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Rest assured that MTI, ESG, in fact, together with EMA, as well as our colleagues in NEA and MSE, we are very committed to supporting our SMEs across various sectors to embark on their sustainability journey, be it at the system level, or be it taking the first few steps by adopting energy efficient equipment.
